description: The plot illustrates the training loss over steps for six different model configurations—ChemBART Small 20M, ChemBERTa Small 20M, ChemBERTa Medium 20M, ChemLLaMA Small 20M, and ChemLLaMA Medium 20M—trained on a 20M data size, as described in the paper “The Role of Model Architecture and Scale in Predicting Molecular Properties: Insights from Fine-Tuning RoBERTa, BART, and LLaMA.” The x-axis, labeled “Step,” spans from 0K to 440K, with major tick marks at 0K, 20K, 40K, 60K, 80K, 420K, 430K, and 440K, indicating a non-uniform scale that zooms in on the final 20K steps (from 420K to 440K) in an inset. The y-axis, labeled “Train Loss,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.85, with major gridlines at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.75, and 0.85. All six lines begin near 0.85 at 0K steps and exhibit a steep decline in the first 20K steps, after which the rate of decline slows. By 80K steps, all lines have converged to values below 0.2, with ChemLLaMA Medium 20M (brown) and ChemLLaMA Small 20M (purple) showing the lowest loss, hovering around 0.05–0.10. In the zoomed-in region (420K–440K), all lines remain relatively flat and close together, with ChemLLaMA Medium 20M maintaining the lowest loss (~0.03), followed closely by ChemLLaMA Small 20M (~0.04), while ChemBERTa Small 20M (green) and ChemBART Small 20M (red) show slightly higher and more noisy loss values (~0.06–0.07). The lines are solid with no markers, and each is color-coded as indicated in the legend.
